```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(rvis)

# The examples below use chart types also provided by billboarder, c3, and
# plotly. Change this value to one of those wrapper prefixes to try another
# plotter with the same data and arguments.
plotter <- "amCharts"
plotter_package <- switch(
  plotter,
  amCharts = "rAmCharts",
  billboarder = "billboarder",
  c3 = "c3",
  plotly = "plotly",
  stop("Choose amCharts, billboarder, c3, or plotly for these examples.")
)

if (!requireNamespace(plotter_package, quietly = TRUE)) {
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
}
```

`rvisPlot()` dispatches to a wrapper using the `plotter` prefix and chart
`type`. The following examples use bar, pie, and time-series line charts,
which are available in all four plotter wrappers listed above. The default
`plotter` value calls `amCharts.bar()`, `amCharts.pie()`, and
`amCharts.tsline()`.

## Bar chart

The built-in `iris` data provides a small example without external data files.
The data is summarized first so each species has one bar.

```{r bar}
species_means <- aggregate(Petal.Length ~ Species, data = iris, FUN = mean)

rvisPlot(
  type = "bar", plotter = plotter, obj = species_means,
  x = "Species", y = "Petal.Length",
  config = list(title = "Mean petal length by species")
)
```

## Pie chart

The pie wrapper uses a label column and a numeric `theta` column.

```{r pie}
rvisPlot(
  type = "pie", plotter = plotter, obj = species_means,
  label = "Species", theta = "Petal.Length",
  config = list(title = "Mean petal length")
)
```

## Time-series line chart

This synthetic series has a POSIXct time column, which the amCharts wrapper
expects. The other listed wrappers accept this same input or coerce it to
their supported date representation.

```{r time-series}
time_data <- data.frame(
  time = as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC") + (0:23) * 30 * 24 * 60 * 60,
  observed = 20 + sin((0:23) * pi / 6) * 5 + (0:23) * 0.3,
  forecast = 20 + sin((0:23) * pi / 6) * 4 + (0:23) * 0.35
)

rvisPlot(
  type = "tsline", plotter = plotter, obj = time_data,
  x = "time", y = list(observed = "observed", forecast = "forecast"),
  config = list(title = "Observed and forecast values")
)
```

To try another compatible wrapper, change only the `plotter` assignment in
the setup chunk to `"billboarder"`, `"c3"`, or `"plotly"` (and install that
plotter package). Other amCharts chart types, such as gauges and bullet
charts, have their own input conventions and are not covered by these
cross-plotter examples.
